item.title: Unpatched Cacti 1.2.31 bug lets anonymous guests reach code execution, and exploit code is public
item.guid: 2026-11-28|https://gbhackers.com/cacti-4http2root-zero-day/|Unpatched Cacti 1.2.31 bug lets anonymous guests reach code execution, and exploit code is public
item.description: [Critical (no CVE yet)] A researcher disclosed '4HTTP2ROOT' on November 26, a second-order SQL injection in Cacti where input stored through anonymous guest access is later used in a query, letting an attacker alter polling configuration and run commands. There is no patch, CVE or CVSS score yet; Previdian (tracking it as VULN-2026-0010) reproduced the public PoC, and no in-the-wild exploitation was confirmed at disclosure. Disable the guest user in Authentication Settings and the guest account under Users, keep Cacti reachable only from management networks or VPN, drop unneeded root privileges from its poller, and rotate device credentials Cacti holds if you see unexpected settings or polling changes. (Source: GBHackers)

item.title: NFS2ROOT: 12-year-old Linux nfsd heap overflow gives unauthenticated remote root on exposed NFS servers
item.guid: 2026-11-28|https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/new-nfs2root-linux-flaw-can-let-attackers-gain-root-privileges/|NFS2ROOT: 12-year-old Linux nfsd heap overflow gives unauthenticated remote root on exposed NFS servers
item.description: [Critical · CVE-2026-99362] CVE-2026-99362 is a heap buffer overflow in the kernel NFS server, present since 3.16, that a remote attacker can trigger with crafted NFSv4.1/4.2 requests to leak memory, defeat KASLR and run a command as root, with no credentials or user interaction. Kernels older than 6.12.117, 6.18.61, 7.3.2 or 7.4-rc1 are affected when nfsd is running and TCP 2049 is reachable; OpenSec built a full exploit and shared it with maintainers, but no exploitation in the wild has been reported. Install your distro's kernel update and reboot, limit port 2049 to trusted clients until then, and disable nfs-server where it is not needed. (Source: BleepingComputer)

item.title: SAP confirms an incident after reports that stolen employee tokens were used to copy and alter code on GitHub
item.guid: 2026-11-28|https://www.securityweek.com/sap-confirms-cyberattack-source-code-reportedly-compromised/|SAP confirms an incident after reports that stolen employee tokens were used to copy and alter code on GitHub
item.description: SAP says it detected suspicious activity and took urgent action, and has so far found no sign that customer business data was accessed; German media citing insiders report attackers took employee authentication tokens and used them to copy and modify source code in SAP's GitHub environment. Handelsblatt reports SAP is rotating signing keys, restricting GitHub access and pausing automated development pipelines, and nothing so far shows tampered code reached customer deliveries. If you consume SAP's public GitHub repos or samples, pin to known commits and verify signatures on anything pulled recently, and treat this as another reminder to scope and expire developer tokens tightly. (Source: SecurityWeek)

item.title: North Korea-linked PolinRider has planted a blockchain-driven Python loader in thousands of GitHub repositories
item.guid: 2026-11-28|https://thehackernews.com/2026/11/north-korea-linked-polinrider-poisons.html|North Korea-linked PolinRider has planted a blockchain-driven Python loader in thousands of GitHub repositories
item.description: [High] PolinRider hides a loader in small utils modules or conftest.py files; when Python imports it, it reads an Ethereum transaction to fetch JavaScript, runs it with Node.js and opens a session to a C2 server such as 103.179.142[.]155 or 95.135.181[.]84. SafeDep found it in 375 public repos and Apiiro estimates at least 7,609 repos across 2,330 accounts, spread through force-pushed commits from compromised developer machines, malicious pull requests, fake job sites and a rogue VS Code extension. Review recent commits and PRs that touch conftest.py or utility packages, alert on Python processes spawning node, and rotate secrets on developer machines that ran affected code. (Source: The Hacker News)

item.title: llama.cpp fixes a CVSS 9.8 out-of-bounds write in its unauthenticated RPC server, the third critical RPC bug in weeks
item.guid: 2026-11-28|https://app.opencve.io/cve/CVE-2026-137567|llama.cpp fixes a CVSS 9.8 out-of-bounds write in its unauthenticated RPC server, the third critical RPC bug in weeks
item.description: [Critical 9.8 · CVE-2026-137567] CVE-2026-137567 lets anyone who can reach the ggml rpc-server write to arbitrary heap addresses by sending a copy_tensor command with a zero-element destination tensor, which can crash the server or lead to code execution. Builds b11450 up to b12657 are affected and b12658 fixes it; it is not in KEV and no exploitation has been reported. Upgrade every host running rpc-server, bind it to localhost or a private inference-only segment (default port 50052), since the RPC service has no authentication at all. (Source: OpenCVE)

item.title: Shadowserver counts about 4,200 internet-exposed AI hacking-framework servers, most of them ARTEX
item.guid: 2026-11-28|https://cybersecuritynews.com/4000-servers-running-ai-hacking-agents-are-exposed/|Shadowserver counts about 4,200 internet-exposed AI hacking-framework servers, most of them ARTEX
item.description: Shadowserver saw roughly 4,200 exposed instances of agentic attack frameworks on November 23, up from just under 3,700 a day earlier, with ARTEX making up about 70%, and logged over 10,000 honeypot events from more than 80 source IPs between November 9 and 23. About one in ten sources sent exploit or injection attempts, most often against the old Metabase flaw CVE-2023-38646. Patch internet-facing apps with known exploited bugs first, rate-limit bursty scanning, and if you find one of these frameworks on your own network, confirm it is an approved deployment and lock it behind a VPN and strong authentication, or isolate it and investigate. (Source: Cyber Security News)

item.title: Update: Drupal discloses a second installer takeover bug, CVE-2026-136716, already exploited on sites patched for Fail2Install
item.guid: 2026-11-27|https://thehackernews.com/2026/11/drupal-warns-of-new-highly-critical.html|Update: Drupal discloses a second installer takeover bug, CVE-2026-136716, already exploited on sites patched for Fail2Install
item.description: [Highly critical · CVE-2026-136716 · CVE-2026-132165] Drupal says a new core flaw is being exploited to take over sites whose installer was still reachable after the fix for last week's Fail2Install bug (CVE-2026-132165); sites that locked down install.php are not affected. Fixes are in 11.4.14, 11.3.23 and 10.6.23, while 11.0-11.2 and 10.5 and older are end-of-life and get nothing. Update and run update.php, block access to the installer, and check logs for changes to or by user 1, confirming its email is yours and resetting its password if in doubt. (Source: The Hacker News)

item.title: CISA adds 10 exploited flaws to KEV, including five Mitel MiCollab AWV bugs and a Xen Orchestra token auth bypass
item.guid: 2026-11-27|https://thehackernews.com/2026/11/hackers-exploit-10-vulnerabilities.html|CISA adds 10 exploited flaws to KEV, including five Mitel MiCollab AWV bugs and a Xen Orchestra token auth bypass
item.description: [Critical 10.0 · CVE-2026-133323 · CVE-2026-133303 · CVE-2026-133275 · CVE-2026-133311 · CVE-2026-133324 · CVE-2026-133469 · CVE-2023-25914 · CVE-2023-25915 · CVE-2025-41450 · CVE-2026-103406] The November 25 KEV batch covers five Mitel MiCollab AWV flaws (led by a CVSS 10 command injection and a 9.0 XML injection), a 9.8 Xen Orchestra authentication bypass using a crafted token, three Danfoss AK-SM 800A controller bugs, and the Juniper Session Smart Conductor injection we covered yesterday. Federal agencies must fix most of them by November 28 and the remaining two by December 9. Move MiCollab to 10.3.0.18 or later (or cut external access to AWV), patch Xen Orchestra, and keep Danfoss controllers behind a VPN in Strict mode; since patching does not remove an existing foothold, check exposed MiCollab servers for staged files. (Source: The Hacker News)

item.title: Update: Singapore's CSA says the NGINX HTTP/2 heap overflow with public PoCs is now reportedly exploited
item.guid: 2026-11-27|https://www.csa.gov.sg/alerts-and-advisories/alerts/al-2026-168/|Update: Singapore's CSA says the NGINX HTTP/2 heap overflow with public PoCs is now reportedly exploited
item.description: [High 8.1 · CVE-2026-123007 · CVE-2026-123633] A November 26 CSA alert says CVE-2026-123007, the HTTP/2 flow-control heap overflow in NGINX that researchers released proof-of-concept code for last week, is reportedly being exploited; a companion worker use-after-free (CVE-2026-123633) is not listed as exploited. Affected builds are NGINX Open Source 1.9.5 up to 1.30.7 and 1.31.0 up to 1.31.9, plus NGINX Plus R34-R36 and 37.x before 37.0.8.1 or 37.3.0.1. Upgrade now with a full restart rather than a reload, check distro-packaged NGINX separately, and turn off HTTP/2 where patching has to wait. (Source: Cyber Security Agency of Singapore)

item.title: watchTowr sees probes for two newly disclosed GeoServer bugs as researchers publish unauthenticated RCE chains
item.guid: 2026-11-27|https://www.securityweek.com/two-newly-disclosed-geoserver-vulnerabilities-under-attack/|watchTowr sees probes for two newly disclosed GeoServer bugs as researchers publish unauthenticated RCE chains
item.description: [High · CVE-2026-120705 · CVE-2026-129243 · CVE-2026-129245 · CVE-2026-120704 · CVE-2026-129244 · CVE-2026-129242] GeoServer published advisories on November 24 for a set of flaws, and watchTowr's honeypots caught error-based probes for the WFS XML injection (CVE-2026-120705) and the service-rule access bypass (CVE-2026-129243) within a day, aimed at finding vulnerable servers rather than achieving code execution so far. Eye Security and Rapid7 have each shown chains, one using a predictable remember-me signing key (CVE-2026-129245), that reach unauthenticated RCE, and a public PoC exists. Upgrade to GeoServer 3.0.2, 2.28.6 or 2.27.7, restrict internet access to instances you cannot patch quickly, and check for credential leaks or unexpected admin sessions. (Source: SecurityWeek)

item.title: WordPress.org closes six WP Connect plugins after backdoored releases were caught before going out
item.guid: 2026-11-27|https://thehackernews.com/2026/11/wordpress-blocks-six-backdoored-wp.html|WordPress.org closes six WP Connect plugins after backdoored releases were caught before going out
item.description: [Critical 9.8 · CVE-2026-135202] After the developer account behind WP Connect appears to have been compromised, WordPress.org closed six of its Airtable, Notion, Brevo and Contact Form 7 integration plugins (about 3,600 installs) and stopped the malicious updates from being released. The planted file, includes/airwp-online.php, would have called out to tascredit-pay[.]com on every request and run returned PHP, giving full file, shell and database control. Sites are unlikely to have received the backdoor, but anyone using Air WP Sync, WP Sync for Notion or the other closed plugins should remove them, since they will get no further fixes, and look for that file and odd WP-Cron hooks. (Source: The Hacker News)

item.title: Socket finds 13 malicious NuGet packages posing as WinUI and WPF button controls in fake .NET job tests
item.guid: 2026-11-27|https://thehackernews.com/2026/11/13-malicious-nuget-packages-turn-fake.html|Socket finds 13 malicious NuGet packages posing as WinUI and WPF button controls in fake .NET job tests
item.description: Socket found 13 NuGet packages, including WinUI.Button, VS_Builder.WinUI3Controls, HappyOne.MSBuildAnalyzer and WinUI3IconButton, that were handed to developers as part of fake take-home assessments and used MSBuild targets to drop a sideloaded DLL and further payloads at build time. The same operators ran lookalike axios repos on GitHub and npm packages such as axios-native and fs-extra-core; NuGet has removed all 13 packages. Treat unsolicited coding tests as untrusted code, build them only in a throwaway VM, and search build hosts for the listed package IDs and for %LOCALAPPDATA%\osk\OskSupport.dll. (Source: The Hacker News)

item.title: Microsoft says Chinese and North Korean state groups now run intrusions with the ARTEX agentic pentest framework
item.guid: 2026-11-27|https://www.techradar.com/pro/security/microsoft-says-chinese-and-north-korean-hacking-groups-are-now-actively-using-artex-in-their-attacks|Microsoft says Chinese and North Korean state groups now run intrusions with the ARTEX agentic pentest framework
item.description: In a November 25 report, Microsoft says China-linked groups including Salt Typhoon and Crystal Typhoon, North Korean actors and financially motivated crews are using the AI-driven ARTEX framework for reconnaissance, credential attacks and exploitation, and notes a clone called AntiFox. Because the agents work at machine speed and the default artex-enrich user agent is easy to change, signature detection alone will miss them. Alert on bursts of high-rate activity from single sources, harden identity protections, and put decoys in place to catch automated recon. (Source: TechRadar)

item.title: Google will require AI agents to reach Workspace data only through its MCP servers or CLI from February 2027
item.guid: 2026-11-27|https://www.helpnetsecurity.com/2026/11/26/google-ai-agent-security-requirements/|Google will require AI agents to reach Workspace data only through its MCP servers or CLI from February 2027
item.description: From February 1, 2027, autonomous agents must use Google's now generally available Workspace MCP servers or CLI under a new AI Tools Addendum, with dedicated OAuth client IDs, narrower scopes and quotas; ordinary apps can keep using REST APIs. On Google Cloud, Agent Gateway adds IAM enforcement, default-deny egress and Model Armor prompt-injection screening, and the addendum bans training on or permanently storing raw Workspace data. Admins should inventory connected agents and OAuth grants now, and developers should move agent integrations over and add user confirmation and injection defenses before the deadline. (Source: Help Net Security)

item.title: Juniper now reports exploitation of the unauthenticated Session Smart Conductor command injection; upgrade to 7.0.5, 7.1.7 or 7.2.3
item.guid: 2026-11-26|https://securityonline.info/juniper-session-smart-router-vulnerabilities/|Juniper now reports exploitation of the unauthenticated Session Smart Conductor command injection; upgrade to 7.0.5, 7.1.7 or 7.2.3
item.description: [Critical 9.8 · CVE-2026-103406] Juniper updated bulletin JSA112183 on November 24 to say at least one malicious exploitation of CVE-2026-103406 has been reported to its SIRT; the October advisory had said no attacks were known. The bug lets an unauthenticated attacker run OS commands on Session Smart Conductor during key management, and the same bulletin fixes a 9.8 admin-takeover flaw in Session Smart Router (CVE-2026-103409). There is no workaround, so move to 7.0.5, 7.1.7, 7.2.3 or later and keep Conductor and router management interfaces off untrusted networks until you do. (Source: SecurityOnline)

item.title: Attackers used a CVSS 10 deserialization bug in the hex.pm registry server to run commands on six production hosts
item.guid: 2026-11-26|https://thehackernews.com/2026/11/hackers-exploited-cvss-100-hexpm-rce.html|Attackers used a CVSS 10 deserialization bug in the hex.pm registry server to run commands on six production hosts
item.description: [Critical 10.0 · CVE-2026-129514 · CVE-2026-124283 · CVE-2026-133555 · CVE-2026-130411] The Elixir/Erlang package registry hex.pm disclosed that its server accepted Erlang-format request bodies containing struct maps before routing and authentication, a check removed back in 2016, which chained into OS command execution; the attacker sent 69 exploit requests and got code running on six servers before everything was patched. The team's audit found no tampered packages, but it cannot rule out reads of account data such as emails, password hashes and 2FA secrets, so all sessions were revoked. Hex users should change their password, reset 2FA and re-authenticate the client, fetch only from repo.hex.pm until the updated client ships, and anyone self-hosting the hexpm server should deploy the fix; related library fixes landed in ash 3.38.0, db_connection 2.10.3 and new flop releases. (Source: The Hacker News)

item.title: 1Password says a hijacked employee GitHub account let an attacker plant code in backend services and pull customer account records
item.guid: 2026-11-26|https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/1password-customer-data-stolen-after-employee-github-account-breach/|1Password says a hijacked employee GitHub account let an attacker plant code in backend services and pull customer account records
item.description: 1Password found on November 19 that an employee's corporate GitHub account had been compromised and used to reach private repositories, reach the CI/CD environment and inject code into backend services that collected customer account metadata such as names, emails, IDs, public keys, SRP parameters and invitation or recovery tokens. The company says vaults and their encryption keys were not exposed, a small number of customers were notified, the stolen token was revoked and infrastructure credentials were rotated. It is a reminder to treat developer GitHub identities and CI secrets as production credentials: enforce phishing-resistant MFA and short-lived tokens, and alert on code pushed to deploy paths from unusual sessions; 1Password customers should watch for unexpected invitations, recovery requests and phishing. (Source: BleepingComputer)

item.title: Update: Palo Alto ships PAN-OS fixes for the Fragnesia kernel bug that PHP2Shell attackers used to root firewalls
item.guid: 2026-11-26|https://www.securityweek.com/palo-alto-networks-patches-fragnesia-flaw-used-to-root-firewalls/|Update: Palo Alto ships PAN-OS fixes for the Fragnesia kernel bug that PHP2Shell attackers used to root firewalls
item.description: [Exploited · CVE-2026-46300 · CVE-2026-109618] Palo Alto Networks published PAN-SA-2026-0015 with fixed PAN-OS builds across the 10.2, 11.1, 11.2, 12.1 and 12.2 trains for CVE-2026-46300, the Linux kernel ESP-in-TCP privilege escalation that a China-linked group chained after PHP2Shell RCE to get root on 25 servers. The vendor says the only known path to exploiting it is first compromising an internet-exposed management interface via PHP2Shell. Install the hotfix for your train, confirm the October PHP2Shell patches are in place, and restrict management interfaces to a dedicated network or VPN. (Source: SecurityWeek)

item.title: Eclypsium: most exploited flaws fixed in network appliance advisories last month sat in bundled PHP, Node.js and OpenSSH
item.guid: 2026-11-26|https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/infratrust-warns-of-exploited-supply-chain-flaws-in-network-appliances/|Eclypsium: most exploited flaws fixed in network appliance advisories last month sat in bundled PHP, Node.js and OpenSSH
item.description: [CVE-2026-109618 · CVE-2026-109619 · CVE-2026-76466 · CVE-2026-114625 · CVE-2026-19868] Eclypsium's InfraTrust Pulse reviewed 373 advisories from 23 infrastructure vendors between mid-October and November 19 and found 38 that addressed CISA KEV flaws, 33 of them in third-party components the vendors ship inside their appliances. PHP2Shell fixes were still partial or missing for several vendors as of November 20, and the report's priority list includes Cisco Expressway, Arista VeloCloud Orchestrator, Cisco ASA/FTD VPN and SonicWall SSO VPN bugs already exploited in the wild. Track bundled-component CVEs per appliance rather than per vendor, take management interfaces off the internet, and check devices that were exposed for backdoors that survive patching. (Source: BleepingComputer)

item.title: GreyNoise tracks an agent-driven actor that has compromised 24 Check Point management servers across at least 22 organizations
item.guid: 2026-11-26|https://www.securityweek.com/check-point-security-management-servers-hacked-in-ai-assisted-campaign/|GreyNoise tracks an agent-driven actor that has compromised 24 Check Point management servers across at least 22 organizations
item.description: GreyNoise says the actor it calls GT13 uses agentic harnesses to scan and exploit automatically from 99 IP addresses, with some hands-on-keyboard work, and has hit energy, finance, government, manufacturing and transport targets in several countries since early October. In one victim it tried a long list of old and new CVEs across Citrix, Ivanti, Exchange, vCenter, NetLogon and Check Point SmartConsole, which shows how cheaply AI tooling lets an attacker cycle through known bugs. Patch the whole edge and management estate rather than just the latest headline CVE, and review Check Point Security Management servers for unexpected admin sessions; GreyNoise believes the campaign is ongoing. (Source: SecurityWeek)

item.title: Swiss NCSC confirms its first AI-agent intrusions, hitting critical infrastructure operators in at least two sectors
item.guid: 2026-11-26|https://securityaffairs.com/204004/hacking/switzerland-confirms-first-ai-agent-cyberattacks-on-local-organisations.html|Swiss NCSC confirms its first AI-agent intrusions, hitting critical infrastructure operators in at least two sectors
item.description: Switzerland's NCSC says it received its first reports of attacks run with agentic offensive frameworks, and in every case it knows of the attackers got into the victims' systems through weak passwords, known flaws or exposed services. It notes that internet-reachable instances of agent tools such as ARTEX and CyberStrikeAI have nearly doubled since October. Its advice is basic but now urgent: shrink exposure with allow-lists or geo-blocking, put webmail and VPN behind MFA or passkeys, enforce least privilege, watch for unusual data volumes, and patch critical internet-facing flaws within 24 hours of release. (Source: Security Affairs)

item.title: Decoy container images show bots using AWS keys leaked in public registries within seconds and draining LLM API credit
item.guid: 2026-11-26|https://www.helpnetsecurity.com/2026/11/25/docker-aws-key-exposure-bots/|Decoy container images show bots using AWS keys leaked in public registries within seconds and draining LLM API credit
item.description: Stony Brook University researchers pushed 300 nginx look-alike images carrying decoy AWS, OpenAI and Anthropic keys to eight registries; the AWS keys drew over 140,000 API calls from more than 5,000 IPs, with a median of 51 seconds and a fastest of under 8 seconds to first use. The bots watch newest-image listings and pull only the layers likely to hold credentials, and the LLM keys had their balances drained. Keep secrets out of image layers entirely (use build secrets and multi-stage builds), scan images before pushing, scope keys tightly, and rotate immediately if one ever ships in an image. (Source: Help Net Security)

item.title: WHMCS patches an unauthenticated cart SQL injection that exposes client data and admin password hashes
item.guid: 2026-11-26|https://thehackernews.com/2026/11/whmcs-sql-injection-flaw-could-expose.html|WHMCS patches an unauthenticated cart SQL injection that exposes client data and admin password hashes
item.description: [High 8.7 · CVE-2026-82981 · CVE-2026-82979 · CVE-2026-93700] WHMCS fixed three flaws: a no-login SQL injection in the shopping cart (CVE-2026-82981), an authenticated Client Area SQL injection, and an email-campaign bug rated 9.0 that lets a logged-in client read configuration files including database credentials and possibly run code. Fixes are in 9.0.10 and 8.13.8, with 9.1.2 announced for the 9.1 line; 8.0 to 8.12 get no patch, and no attacks have been reported yet. Self-hosted operators should upgrade now, then delete planned or running email campaigns and empty the template cache as the advisory instructs. (Source: The Hacker News)

item.title: OpenAI and Cisco open-source Shirudo, where AI agents write signed eBPF shields to block exploits until a patch lands
item.guid: 2026-11-26|https://thehackernews.com/2026/11/openai-and-cisco-unveil-ai-assisted.html|OpenAI and Cisco open-source Shirudo, where AI agents write signed eBPF shields to block exploits until a patch lands
item.description: Shirudo is a Linux runtime built on Tetragon in which AI agents draft eBPF rules that block a specific exploit path without restarting the service; shields are signed, verified via TPM on the host, start in monitor-only mode and need operator approval before they block. In a demo, a Codex-generated shield stopped a Java4Shell attempt against a live Elasticsearch service. It is an early, interesting model for AI-assisted virtual patching, but treat agent-written kernel policy like any other change: review it, stage it in monitor mode, and keep the real patch on schedule. (Source: The Hacker News)

item.title: Update: Drupal installer takeover bug is now exploited on live sites and in CISA KEV, due November 27
item.guid: 2026-11-25|https://rescana.com/post/drupal-core-installer-flaw-cve-2026-132165-exploited-and-in-cisa-kev-update-now|Update: Drupal installer takeover bug is now exploited on live sites and in CISA KEV, due November 27
item.description: [Drupal: Highly critical 20/25 · CVE-2026-132165] The Drupal core flaw that lets an unauthenticated visitor re-run core/install.php and take over a site (SA-CORE-2026-017) moved from patched to actively exploited: Drupal's security team got reports of attacks on live sites from November 19, and CISA added it to KEV on November 24 with a November 27 deadline for federal agencies. Exploitation needs an uncommon configuration, but it requires no login. Upgrade to 10.6.22, 11.3.22 or 11.4.13 now; sites on end-of-life branches get no fix, so block or delete install.php at the web server and plan the upgrade. Check access logs for requests to install.php since November 19. (Source: Rescana)

item.title: CISA adds N-able Mail Assure SSRF and the MONAI Label path traversal to KEV, both due November 26
item.guid: 2026-11-25|https://securityaffairs.com/203882/hacking/u-s-cisa-adds-n-able-mailassure-and-project-monai-flaws-to-its-known-exploited-vulnerabilities-catalog.html|CISA adds N-able Mail Assure SSRF and the MONAI Label path traversal to KEV, both due November 26
item.description: [Critical 9.8 / 9.3 · CVE-2026-134624 · CVE-2026-133968] CISA put two flaws in KEV: the MONAI Label path traversal (CVE-2026-133968, CVSS 9.8, fixed in 0.8.6) that AI-agent-driven attackers used against universities, and an SSRF in N-able Mail Assure / SpamExperts LDAP sync checks (CVE-2026-134624, CVSS 9.3) found while N-able investigated a breach of a Hosted Cloud server. N-able has patched its hosted platform (build 20261121.1943), revoked customer API and OAuth tokens, and says it has not confirmed the SSRF was the way in. Hosted customers should re-issue credentials for any scripts or integrations; SpamExperts Local Cloud operators should confirm they are on build 20261121.1943, and MONAI Label users should upgrade and keep it off the internet. (Source: Security Affairs)

item.title: VMware fixes 23 flaws including a CVSS 9.8 vCenter Directory Service auth bypass and two critical ESX I/O filter bugs
item.guid: 2026-11-25|https://www.securityweek.com/vmware-updates-patch-critical-esx-vcenter-vulnerabilities/|VMware fixes 23 flaws including a CVSS 9.8 vCenter Directory Service auth bypass and two critical ESX I/O filter bugs
item.description: [Critical 9.8 · CVE-2026-123903 · CVE-2026-123910 · CVE-2026-123911 · CVE-2026-123912] Broadcom's VMSA-2026-0011 covers vCenter, ESX, VMware Tools, Workstation, Fusion and Avi Load Balancer, headlined by an authentication bypass in the vCenter Directory Service and a heap overflow and use-after-free in the ESX I/O filter service, all rated 9.8, plus a 9.3 XHCI USB bug that lets a VM admin run code in the VMX process. Broadcom does not list any of these as exploited, but vCenter has been a repeat target this month, so treat it as urgent. Patch vCenter first (8.0 U3m or the 9.1.x fix), then ESX and the desktop products, and handle the separate SDDC Manager updates from VMSA-2026-0009. (Source: SecurityWeek)

item.title: Rackspace is shutting down its Spot managed Kubernetes service after attackers read customer cluster Secrets
item.guid: 2026-11-25|https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/rackspace-shuts-down-spot-cloud-platform-after-security-breach/|Rackspace is shutting down its Spot managed Kubernetes service after attackers read customer cluster Secrets
item.description: An attacker with compromised credentials created pods in Rackspace Spot customer clusters on November 17, read Kubernetes Secrets and could reach files on storage volumes; Rackspace restored service on November 21 but will terminate the platform on December 8. Spot customers should treat API and refresh tokens, kubeconfigs and every cluster Secret as exposed and rotate them, review logs back to November 16, and look for pods or objects with the prefixes i1, glm- or probe and connections from 23.224.79[.]106 or 23.224.0[.]0/15. Move workloads and download data before the deadline. (Source: BleepingComputer)

item.title: binary-parser for npm lets attacker-controlled parser definitions inject JavaScript; incomplete fix for an earlier CVE
item.guid: 2026-11-25|https://thehackernews.com/2026/11/critical-binary-parser-flaw-enables.html|binary-parser for npm lets attacker-controlled parser definitions inject JavaScript; incomplete fix for an earlier CVE
item.description: [Critical 9.2 · CVE-2026-134814] The binary-parser npm package dropped several string options (length, lengthInBytes, key, tag, offset and the namely() alias) straight into the JavaScript it generates, so anyone who controls a parser definition can run code in the Node.js process when it compiles. This is an incomplete fix for CVE-2026-1245 from January; parsing untrusted data with a trusted definition is not affected, and there is no report of exploitation. Upgrade to 2.3.1, which rejects expressions in those options, and treat any parser definition from outside your code as executable. (Source: The Hacker News)

item.title: WebSec benchmark: search APIs used by coding agents returned known-malicious results in about 1.4% of searches
item.guid: 2026-11-25|https://labs.cloudsecurityalliance.org/research/csa-research-note-search-api-poisoning-coding-agents-2026112/|WebSec benchmark: search APIs used by coding agents returned known-malicious results in about 1.4% of searches
item.description: AIR Research Lab ran about 37,700 searches through eight commercial search APIs that AI coding agents rely on and found 534 surfaced known-malicious content, with install and package-selection queries the riskiest; one example was a starred GitHub repo whose README PowerShell one-liner installed a NetSupport RAT. The Cloud Security Alliance notes the benchmark is vendor-produced and not yet replicated, but the pattern matches real agent compromises. Treat search results and READMEs as untrusted input, require human approval for download-and-execute commands (curl|sh, iwr|iex), check package age and registry presence before installs, and keep agent runtimes away from credentials. (Source: Cloud Security Alliance)

item.title: CERT-In warns AI-assisted intruders are altering approval workflows to push unauthorized payments at Indian banks and fintechs
item.guid: 2026-11-25|https://thehackernews.com/2026/11/ai-assisted-cyberattacks-trigger.html|CERT-In warns AI-assisted intruders are altering approval workflows to push unauthorized payments at Indian banks and fintechs
item.description: CERT-In advisory CIAD-2026-0062 describes attackers, helped by AI agent frameworks such as ARTEX, PentAGI, CAIRN and CyberStrikeAI, changing business records and approval relationships inside banks, NBFCs and payment providers so that legitimate disbursement processes sent multi-crore sums to mule accounts without tripping alerts. The abuse targets business logic rather than payment APIs. Verify changes to payee records and approval chains, tighten reconciliation, make sure monitoring covers misuse of trusted workflows, and patch internet-facing AI apps such as Langflow and RAGFlow; one related CyberStrikeAI IP is 43.240.29[.]11. (Source: The Hacker News)

item.title: Mandiant sees attackers exploiting a deserialization bug in the long-abandoned Idunno.AntiCsrf ASP.NET module for pre-auth RCE
item.guid: 2026-11-24|https://thehackernews.com/2026/11/hackers-exploit-critical-aspnet-anti.html|Mandiant sees attackers exploiting a deserialization bug in the long-abandoned Idunno.AntiCsrf ASP.NET module for pre-auth RCE
item.description: [Critical 9.3 · CVE-2026-131914] Idunno.AntiCsrf 0.9.1 (including the 0.9.1 Beta), a third-party anti-CSRF module for classic ASP.NET that has not been updated since 2008, deserializes untrusted input, so one unauthenticated POST can run code inside the IIS worker process. Mandiant says it has seen this exploited in the wild, and there is no patch because the project is dead. Search Web.config files and bin/ folders for Idunno.AntiCsrf or AntiCsrfModule, replace it with ASP.NET's built-in anti-forgery features, and look in IIS logs for odd POSTs to .aspx pages that returned 302 or 500. If you find signs of compromise, rotate machineKey values and database credentials and check webroots for files that shouldn't be there. (Source: The Hacker News)

item.title: Norway's NSM says an Azure API Management flaw was used to go after secrets at energy companies
item.guid: 2026-11-24|https://www.securityweek.com/azure-flaw-exploited-to-target-secrets-at-norwegian-energy-firms/|Norway's NSM says an Azure API Management flaw was used to go after secrets at energy companies
item.description: Norway's National Security Authority says an unknown actor abused a weakness in Azure API Management Classic tiers to target tokens, secrets and named values, and Equinor and Skagerak Energi have both reported incidents, though both say they found no evidence of data theft or compromise. Microsoft found the issue on November 18 and closed the access path the next day. The v2 tiers are not affected, and no CVE has been given. If you run APIM Classic, treat named values, identity-provider client secrets, subscription keys and management API tokens as exposed and rotate them, then work out what data could be reached through the service. (Source: SecurityWeek)

item.title: Dragos bait prompts show at least three AI inference providers were breached and leaked customer prompts without noticing
item.guid: 2026-11-24|https://www.securityweek.com/ai-inference-providers-failed-to-detect-hacking-and-prompt-theft-says-dragos/|Dragos bait prompts show at least three AI inference providers were breached and leaked customer prompts without noticing
item.description: From July to November, Dragos sent about two million prompts carrying trackable URLs, hostnames and fake credentials through AI inference providers. The bait was later used by attackers, which showed that at least three providers had been compromised and that customer prompts were being stolen without the providers spotting it. The biggest haul was about 200 AWS test keys taken in late October, and OpenRouter has since dropped three providers. Assume anything sent to a third-party model endpoint could be read by someone else: keep secrets out of prompts and agent context, and choose providers by how well they can detect intrusions. (Source: SecurityWeek)

item.title: pwn.ai turns a Ghostscript font-loading use-after-free into sandbox-escape RCE through uploads in about ten apps
item.guid: 2026-11-24|https://thehackernews.com/2026/11/researchers-demonstrate-ghostscript.html|pwn.ai turns a Ghostscript font-loading use-after-free into sandbox-escape RCE through uploads in about ten apps
item.description: [High 8.5 · CVE-2026-125396] A use-after-free in Ghostscript's font-loading code switches off the -dSAFER sandbox. Researchers at pwn.ai showed it can be reached over the network through print jobs, email and file uploads in about ten applications. Ghostscript 10.08.0, released in September, fixes it, but some distro packages were still vulnerable when the research was published. The public PoC shows only the memory-corruption part, and no attacks have been reported. Find every Ghostscript copy you actually run, including copies inside containers and other apps, and update it. Until then, require authentication on print queues, restrict which file types you accept, and add AppArmor confinement where you can. (Source: The Hacker News)

item.title: Depthfirst details 'phpAfterShell', a session-file corruption path to RCE fixed in last week's PHP releases
item.guid: 2026-11-24|https://www.securityweek.com/phpaftershell-vulnerability-revives-php2shells-attack-path/|Depthfirst details 'phpAfterShell', a session-file corruption path to RCE fixed in last week's PHP releases
item.description: [Critical 9.2 · CVE-2026-126714] Depthfirst has published details of phpAfterShell, which brings back the PHP2Shell attack route. If a PHP process stops partway through writing a session file to default file storage (most easily triggered through upload-progress tracking), a later session_start() can load the corrupted data and, if the app has a usable deserialization gadget, run code. The fix is in the November 19 releases, PHP 8.5.13, 8.4.28, 8.3.37 and 8.2.36, as well as 8.6.0. No exploitation has been reported. If you haven't installed those releases yet, do so now, and think about turning off session upload progress where you don't use it. (Source: SecurityWeek)

item.title: Elecbrakes trailer brake controllers accept unauthenticated Bluetooth braking commands; the oldest model will not be fixed
item.guid: 2026-11-24|https://www.theregister.com/security/2026/11/23/bluetooth-brakes-are-broken-as-researchers-find-anyone-can-control-them/5311748|Elecbrakes trailer brake controllers accept unauthenticated Bluetooth braking commands; the oldest model will not be fixed
item.description: [Critical 9.6] Element Digital researchers used Claude Code to analyze a decompiled copy of the Elecbrakes app and found that the controllers take braking commands over Bluetooth as plain, unauthenticated bytes. Anyone in radio range could apply the brakes or apply more force than intended. CISA has issued three CVEs, two of them scored 9.6, in advisory ICSA-26-323-02. The in-car and trailer-mounted models have patches that owners must install by hand, but the older ELBC2000 will not get one. For builders of connected devices, the takeaway is to require pairing and message authentication on every safety-critical BLE command, not just some of them. (Source: The Register)

item.title: Attackers used a GL.iNet GoodCloud flaw to plant malware on routers and remote KVMs; some infections date back months
item.guid: 2026-11-23|https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/hackers-exploit-glinet-cloud-flaw-to-infect-routers-kvm-devices/|Attackers used a GL.iNet GoodCloud flaw to plant malware on routers and remote KVMs; some infections date back months
item.description: [Exploited] GL.iNet says an unauthorized party abused a vulnerability in its GoodCloud remote-management service to push malware onto some routers and KVM devices (RM1, RM10, RM1PE, RM4PE, RMQ1 and others); the cloud hole is closed, but that does not clean devices already hit. Analysis of the dropped ni.sh script shows it hides as 'crond -i /tmp/.log', swaps netstat to conceal connections, adds SSH keys and on some units opens root reverse shells, with files dating to December 2025. Check for that process, install the latest security firmware (BleepingComputer lists 1.10.3+ for most RM KVMs and 1.8.7+ for RMQ1; stable router builds were due November 22), reflash without keeping settings if infected, rotate exposed credentials, and examine computers attached to compromised KVMs. Hunt for traffic to 170.39.226[.]219, 66.245.219[.]252 and 65.20.71[.]131. (Source: BleepingComputer)

item.title: GPGME double free triggered by an OpenPGP key with an oversized user ID; update to 2.3.1 and rebuild apps that bundle it
item.guid: 2026-11-23|https://thehackernews.com/2026/11/gnupg-warns-critical-gpgme-flaw-could.html|GPGME double free triggered by an OpenPGP key with an oversized user ID; update to 2.3.1 and rebuild apps that bundle it
item.description: [Critical (vendor) · CVE-2026-129975] GnuPG disclosed a double free in GPGME's status and colon-line parsing: a failed buffer reallocation on a key with a very long user ID leaves a stale pointer that is freed twice, and the project does not rule out remote code execution. Everything using GPGME before 2.3.0 is affected, including mail and XMPP clients, Samba and Gpg4win; no attacks are reported and there is no workaround. Upgrade to GPGME 2.3.1 (or 1.24.4 / the advisory patch on the legacy branch) and Gpg4win 5.1.2 on Windows, and remember that statically linked or bundled copies need a vendor rebuild, not just a system package update. (Source: The Hacker News)

item.title: European Commission confirms AI tools were used in a campaign that knocked HR and payroll systems offline for about ten days
item.guid: 2026-11-23|https://www.brusselstimes.com/2414026/european-commission-confirms-ai-assisted-cyberattack-on-internal-systems-tbtb|European Commission confirms AI tools were used in a campaign that knocked HR and payroll systems offline for about ten days
item.description: A Commission spokesperson confirmed a cyber campaign first detected on October 22 was carried out with AI tools; an EU official told Politico that CERT-EU identified the public ARTEX AI pentest framework, which the Commission itself declined to name. Sysper (pay, leave, timesheets), MyPMO (medical reimbursements) and translation services were disrupted for roughly ten days, and Sysper went down again on November 18; the Commission says it has no evidence of a staff-wide data breach but has not said whether any personal data was taken. Defenders should treat ARTEX-style agent tooling as a real intrusion accelerator: shrink exposed attack surface on internal HR and business apps, alert on rapid automated recon and exploitation, and follow CERT-EU's earlier ARTEX guidance. (Source: The Brussels Times)

item.title: Attackers abused a Microsoft Entra Connect Health API flaw to read tenant metadata; fixed server-side
item.guid: 2026-11-22|https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/microsoft-entra-connect-health-flaw-exploited-to-steal-tenant-data/|Attackers abused a Microsoft Entra Connect Health API flaw to read tenant metadata; fixed server-side
item.description: [Exploited] Microsoft is notifying admins that a bug in the Entra Connect Health API, introduced in July and found on November 9, was exploited for read-only access to tenant-level data such as admin and technical contact emails, tenant IDs, domains, license tier and sync status. A server-side fix went out on November 19; Microsoft says no passwords, tokens or valid keys were exposed and customers do not need to patch anything. It has not said who was behind it or how many tenants were hit, and MSPs report notices for multiple customers. Expect targeted phishing at the exposed admin addresses: enforce phishing-resistant MFA on privileged accounts and review Entra sign-in and audit logs plus Connect Health settings. (Source: BleepingComputer)

item.title: Update: CISA puts vCenter, Apache Roller, Cisco Expressway and an old SAP NetWeaver bug in KEV, due November 23
item.guid: 2026-11-22|https://thehackernews.com/2026/11/hackers-exploit-critical-vmware-cisco.html|Update: CISA puts vCenter, Apache Roller, Cisco Expressway and an old SAP NetWeaver bug in KEV, due November 23
item.description: [KEV · CVE-2026-123890 · CVE-2026-129448 · CVE-2026-76466 · CVE-2025-42884] CISA added four exploited flaws to KEV on November 20: the vCenter auth bypass tied to the Armory Castle espionage group (CVSS 9.8), the pre-auth Apache Roller XML-RPC deserialization RCE (9.8), the Cisco Expressway hard-coded credential root RCE (9.8), and a 2025 SAP NetWeaver Enterprise Portal JNDI injection (6.5). The first three were covered earlier this week; the SAP entry is new, though the article notes no public reporting on how it is being exploited. Federal agencies must remediate by November 23, so treat any unpatched instance of these four as urgent, and apply SAP's November 2025 fix if you have not. (Source: The Hacker News)

item.title: Ruby2Shell: one-byte heap overflow in Ruby case conversion reachable pre-auth via Rails and Sinatra; upgrade Ruby
item.guid: 2026-11-22|https://www.securityweek.com/ruby-patches-ruby2shell-vulnerability-that-could-lead-to-rce/|Ruby2Shell: one-byte heap overflow in Ruby case conversion reachable pre-auth via Rails and Sinatra; upgrade Ruby
item.description: [High 7.4 · CVE-2026-132825] Ruby 4.0.10, 3.4.13 and 3.3.14 fix seven memory-safety bugs in the regex engine and string case mapping, led by Ruby2Shell, an off-by-one heap write when changing case in legacy single-byte encodings such as ISO-8859-1. Researchers say unauthenticated requests can reach it in default Rails and classic Sinatra apps through method-override middleware; versions back to 2.4.0 are affected and EOL 3.2 and older get no fix. No attacks are reported and experts expect real-world RCE to be hard, but a PoC release is planned. Upgrade Ruby, rebuild container images, restart app servers and workers, and check products that bundle their own Ruby (GitLab, GitHub Enterprise Server, Mastodon, Discourse and others) for fixed releases. (Source: SecurityWeek)

item.title: Spring's November fixes include a CVSS 9.8 SpEL injection in Spring Security and filter injection bugs in Spring AI
item.guid: 2026-11-22|https://securityonline.info/spring-security-vulnerabilities-november-2026/|Spring's November fixes include a CVSS 9.8 SpEL injection in Spring Security and filter injection bugs in Spring AI
item.description: [Critical 9.8 · CVE-2026-59273 · CVE-2026-59367 · CVE-2026-123886 · CVE-2026-59378 · CVE-2026-59369 · CVE-2026-59361] The Spring team's November release fixes a batch of flaws; the worst, CVE-2026-59273, is a SpEL injection in Spring Security Web's ELRequestMatcher that can give pre-auth code execution when raw user input reaches the matcher. Others include a fixed admin password in the spring-ldap-test embedded LDAP server that listens on all interfaces (9.4), SpEL injection via Spring Data Elasticsearch @Query (8.8), an Actuator health-path login bypass (8.2), and vector-store filter injection in Spring AI. None are reported exploited. Update to Spring Security 7.1.3/7.0.9, Spring Data Elasticsearch 6.1.3/6.0.9 and Spring AI 2.0.3 (or the matching patched lines), and make sure test LDAP servers are never reachable from untrusted networks. (Source: SecurityOnline)

item.title: One malicious webpage let researchers pull Meta Muse chats, memories and stored credentials; Meta fixed it
item.guid: 2026-11-22|https://thehackernews.com/2026/11/a-single-malicious-webpage-let.html|One malicious webpage let researchers pull Meta Muse chats, memories and stored credentials; Meta fixed it
item.description: NebuSec showed that when Meta's Muse agent browsed an attacker's page, it could send the user's conversation history and saved memories to an outside server without any approval prompt, getting past the Sentinel egress gate. Chaining a bug in Muse's built-in browser with a shared Linux kernel flaw gave root on the user's cloud VM, reaching the credentials Muse holds for connected accounts. This was a lab demonstration, not an in-the-wild attack, and the researchers say every issue was fixed before publication, though Meta has not confirmed it publicly. For teams running browsing agents, it is a reminder to keep credentials out of the agent's runtime and not to trust a single egress filter. (Source: The Hacker News)

item.title: Bell Canada says an 'agentic' threat actor got into a pre-production Maximo system and took enterprise customer data
item.guid: 2026-11-22|https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/bell-canada-says-agentic-hacker-stole-enterprise-customer-data/|Bell Canada says an 'agentic' threat actor got into a pre-production Maximo system and took enterprise customer data
item.description: Bell Canada told enterprise customers that an intruder it calls an 'agentic' threat actor accessed a pre-production environment of its Maximo network-provisioning system on November 17. The data included business contact details, ticket titles and some network-element IP addresses, but Bell says no credentials or sensitive personal information; services were not affected. Bell has not named the actor, explained what 'agentic' means, or said how many customers were hit, and is sharing IOCs privately with customers and the Canadian Centre for Cyber Security. Bell enterprise customers should get those IOCs and watch for phishing that uses the leaked ticket context; everyone else should treat pre-production systems holding real customer data as production. (Source: BleepingComputer)

item.title: 'FastUnlock': public PoC uses Narrator at the Windows lock screen to run programs on a stolen, locked PC; no patch yet
item.guid: 2026-11-21|https://thehackernews.com/2026/11/new-unpatched-windows-0-day-fastunlock.html|'FastUnlock': public PoC uses Narrator at the Windows lock screen to run programs on a stolen, locked PC; no patch yet
item.description: [Unpatched, PoC public] A researcher posting as 'Nightmare Eclipse' released a GitHub proof of concept that abuses Narrator and the Microsoft-account recovery options on the lock screen to launch programs under a limited built-in account, and ThreatLocker confirmed it works. It needs physical access, and TPM-only BitLocker does not help because the drive is already unlocked at the lock screen. There is no CVE or fix and no sign of real-world use yet. Add a BitLocker startup PIN on sensitive laptops, have users shut down or hibernate rather than lock when a device leaves their hands, and watch for a Microsoft update. (Source: The Hacker News)

item.title: Linux KVM use-after-free on AMD hosts with nested virtualization lets a guest reach host memory
item.guid: 2026-11-21|https://thehackernews.com/2026/11/new-linux-kvm-flaw-cve-2026-99312-lets.html|Linux KVM use-after-free on AMD hosts with nested virtualization lets a guest reach host memory
item.description: [High 8.8 · CVE-2026-99312] A dangling pointer left after a nested VM is stopped lets a guest touch freed host memory on AMD KVM hosts with nested virtualization on, which is the kvm_amd default; Intel hosts are not affected. The bug came in with a 2022 fix and was found by Terra Security via DigitalOcean's bug bounty; no exploit is public. Upstream fixes are in 7.3.5, 6.18.64 and 6.12.118, but Debian, Ubuntu and RHEL 9/10 packages were not yet fixed at publication. Patch and reboot hosts (guest updates do nothing), or set kvm_amd nested=0 until a kernel is available. (Source: The Hacker News)

item.title: Amazon: China-nexus operators let Cairn AI agents find and exploit a MONAI Label zero-day to root a university server
item.guid: 2026-11-21|https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/hackers-use-autonomous-ai-tool-cairn-to-find-zero-day-take-over-server/|Amazon: China-nexus operators let Cairn AI agents find and exploit a MONAI Label zero-day to root a university server
item.description: Amazon Threat Intelligence found a publicly exposed instance of the open-source Cairn pentest framework and traced a September campaign against East Asian universities in which autonomous agents went from mapping an API to a working path-traversal file write in MONAI Label in about 11 minutes, then got a root reverse shell via sitecustomize.py. The agents spent hours on failed Redis, Log4Shell, SSRF and credential-spray attempts without human steering. MONAI Label shipped a fix on November 18 (GHSA-qc22-rmgc-vg94); update it and keep AI/ML tooling off the internet. Reported source IPs include 142.4.98[.]145 and 142.4.107[.]34. (Source: BleepingComputer)

item.title: Depthfirst publishes PoCs turning low-privilege database accounts into OS code execution on PostgreSQL, MySQL, Oracle and ClickHouse
item.guid: 2026-11-21|https://thehackernews.com/2026/11/researcher-demonstrates-database-rce.html|Depthfirst publishes PoCs turning low-privilege database accounts into OS code execution on PostgreSQL, MySQL, Oracle and ClickHouse
item.description: [Oracle Text 9.9 · CVE-2026-116331 · CVE-2026-101786 · CVE-2026-114819 · CVE-2026-91609] Researcher Zheng Yu showed that accounts with only object or temp-table creation rights can reach code execution on PostgreSQL (fixed in 18.7, 17.12, 16.16, 15.20, 14.25) and MySQL 26.7.0-26.7.1, and that two Oracle bugs in Oracle Text and ORDS GraphQL chain into an unauthenticated attack; ClickHouse fixed a similar issue without a CVE. No in-the-wild use is reported, but the proofs of concept are public. Apply the October and November fixes, strip the TEMPORARY privilege and temp-table rights from app accounts that do not need them, and keep ORDS endpoints off the internet. (Source: The Hacker News)

item.title: Intruder on an N-able cloud server knocks out Mail Assure and SpamExperts management in three regions
item.guid: 2026-11-21|https://thehackernews.com/2026/11/n-able-confirms-hackers-accessed-cloud.html|Intruder on an N-able cloud server knocks out Mail Assure and SpamExperts management in three regions
item.description: N-able confirmed unauthorized access to one server, with the management portals, APIs, quarantine and logging for Mail Assure and SpamExperts Hosted Cloud down in the Americas, APAC and Europe since November 16; mail filtering itself kept running. The company says it has no evidence of customer data or mailbox access so far and that this is separate from the recent N-central flaws. MSPs and customers on these services should watch for N-able's guidance, expect blind spots in quarantine and logs, and be ready to rotate any API credentials tied to the platform. (Source: The Hacker News)

item.title: Signal now blocks OS-level AI agents like Siri and Gemini from reading chats unless the user opts in
item.guid: 2026-11-21|https://www.theregister.com/security/2026/11/20/signal-slams-door-on-prying-ai-agents-to-protect-privacy/5311466|Signal now blocks OS-level AI agents like Siri and Gemini from reading chats unless the user opts in
item.description: Signal's iOS and Android apps now block screenshots by default, which stops on-device assistants that read the screen from seeing messages; users can turn it off after a warning. Signal says this is only a partial fix because agents may read app data from the file system, and it cannot yet do the same on macOS. For defenders, it is a reminder to inventory which OS assistants and agents have screen or data access on managed devices and to restrict them for sensitive apps. (Source: The Register)

item.title: Research: automated prompt-injection red teams mostly rediscover the same trick; PIPETTE rewards new techniques instead
item.guid: 2026-11-21|https://www.helpnetsecurity.com/2026/11/20/ai-prompt-injection-red-team/|Research: automated prompt-injection red teams mostly rediscover the same trick; PIPETTE rewards new techniques instead
item.description: Researchers from Waterloo, Zhejiang and KTH found that RL-based attack generators produce thousands of 'successful' injections that collapse into a handful of techniques, so agents hardened on them still fail against new ones. Their PIPETTE method groups attacks by technique, rewards novelty and trains agents to check each action against the user's request; on AgentDojo, off-the-shelf attacks succeeded under half a percent of the time with no loss in task completion. When buying AI red-team or guardrail services, ask how many distinct techniques were covered and how the agent holds up against attackers allowed hundreds of attempts. (Source: Help Net Security)

item.title: vCenter directory-service auth bypass was a Chinese APT zero-day for over two months before Broadcom's fix
item.guid: 2026-11-20|https://www.securityweek.com/newly-patched-vmware-vcenter-flaw-exploited-as-zero-day-by-chinese-apt/|vCenter directory-service auth bypass was a Chinese APT zero-day for over two months before Broadcom's fix
item.description: [Critical 9.8 · CVE-2026-123890] Mandiant says the suspected China-nexus group Armory Castle (formerly UNC5221) used a custom tool, Bonesaw, to abuse a VMware Directory Service flaw that turns an unauthenticated network request into an admin session. They then pulled SAML signing material, created an SSO admin, forged tokens, took the vCenter master key and moved on to ESXi; initial access in one case came through a BeyondTrust Remote Support zero-day. Fixes are in vCenter 9.1.1.0200, 9.0.2.0200 and 8.0 U3m, and there is no public patch for end-of-support 7.0. Patch now, and hunt for unexpected SSO admin accounts, forged SAML sessions and signs of LMDB theft. (Source: SecurityWeek)

item.title: Update: clustered Cisco Expressway root RCE exploited soon after a public GitHub PoC, with AI-assisted pivot scripts
item.guid: 2026-11-20|https://www.securityweek.com/hackers-exploit-cisco-expressway-vulnerability-soon-after-poc-release/|Update: clustered Cisco Expressway root RCE exploited soon after a public GitHub PoC, with AI-assisted pivot scripts
item.description: [Critical 9.8 · CVE-2026-76466] Russian firm F6 investigated a breach where attackers rooted two internet-facing Expressway X15.5.3 cluster nodes, pivoted to two internal nodes, and ran custom Python scripts (with comments suggesting AI help) to map SMB shares, poke SQL Server and WinRM, and mine GitLab for credentials. Only clustered Expressway Core and Edge deployments are affected, and Cisco's advisory still does not mention exploitation. Upgrade to X15.5.20 (X14 and older must migrate); if you cannot yet, block TCP 4371-4372 to everything but trusted cluster peers and review the Erlang system logs. (Source: SecurityWeek)

item.title: Update: Java4Shell probing begins as Cisco, Elastic, Red Hat, Atlassian and Siemens publish advisories
item.guid: 2026-11-20|https://www.securityweek.com/java4shell-exploitation-attempts-begin-as-vendors-rush-out-advisories/|Update: Java4Shell probing begins as Cisco, Elastic, Red Hat, Atlassian and Siemens publish advisories
item.description: [Critical (Red Hat) · CVE-2026-114938] GreyNoise, watchTowr, Cloudflare and Previdian all report scanning and blind exploit attempts against the OpenJDK AVX-512 Base64 decoder bug, though no confirmed compromises yet; VulnCheck already offers a full RCE exploit to customers. Vendor status is uneven: Cisco lists more than a dozen affected products with no fix, Siemens says take Industrial Edge Management offline, Elastic says Elasticsearch 7.17.3+ is affected, and Keycloak shipped patched 26.8.2-3 images. Install patched JDK builds and restart Java services; where that is not yet possible, follow vendor workarounds such as disabling AVX-512 on Atlassian Data Center hosts. (Source: SecurityWeek)

item.title: Update: PHP 8.5.13, 8.4.28, 8.3.37 and 8.2.36 land with fixes for 18 CVEs, including PHP-FPM request smuggling
item.guid: 2026-11-20|https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/php-security-updates-fix-18-flaws-including-critical-rce-bugs|Update: PHP 8.5.13, 8.4.28, 8.3.37 and 8.2.36 land with fixes for 18 CVEs, including PHP-FPM request smuggling
item.description: [Critical 9.2 · CVE-2026-129289 · CVE-2026-129474 · CVE-2026-129496 · CVE-2026-126714 · CVE-2026-115560 · CVE-2026-129291 · CVE-2026-128090] The pre-announced PHP security release is out. The headline bug is a PHP-FPM request smuggling flaw (CVSS 9.2) that hits nginx, Apache, HAProxy or LSAPI setups reusing backend connections, alongside several use-after-free and session-handling RCEs and a PHAR signature downgrade; the PHP team says the critical ones need non-default or unusual configurations. Upgrade every supported branch now. Until then, set session.upload_progress.enabled=0, turn off persistent backend connections to PHP-FPM, and keep FPM/LSAPI listeners off untrusted networks. (Source: BleepingComputer)

item.title: Drupal core: anonymous re-run of install.php can lead to site takeover or RCE
item.guid: 2026-11-20|https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/drupal-patches-critical-rce-flaw-warns-exploits-may-surface-quickly/|Drupal core: anonymous re-run of install.php can lead to site takeover or RCE
item.description: [Critical · CVE-2026-132165 · CVE-2026-132166] Drupal fixed a critical core bug that lets an unauthenticated visitor trigger the installer again and take over the site or run code, plus a moderately critical gadget chain that needs admin rights and untrusted deserialization. The security team warned exploits could appear within hours or days. Upgrade to 10.6.22, 11.3.22 or 11.4.13; if you cannot, block /core/install.php at the web server and make sure the server cannot write to or chmod settings.php. (Source: BleepingComputer)

item.title: Splunk fixes about 140 bugs across Enterprise, Enterprise Security and SOAR, five of them critical
item.guid: 2026-11-20|https://www.securityweek.com/splunk-patches-nearly-140-flaws-across-three-core-products/|Splunk fixes about 140 bugs across Enterprise, Enterprise Security and SOAR, five of them critical
item.description: [Critical · CVE-2026-76536 · CVE-2026-76535 · CVE-2026-131202 · CVE-2026-131253 · CVE-2026-131287] Splunk Enterprise has two critical issues that let unauthenticated attackers read or change clustering configuration via an empty shared secret or run arbitrary SPL; Enterprise Security has an ess_admin-to-RCE chain; SOAR has two authenticated RCEs. No exploitation is reported. Upgrade Enterprise to 10.6.1, 10.4.5, 10.2.9, 10.0.12 or 9.4.17, Enterprise Security/PCI app to 8.7.0 and SOAR to 8.8.0, and make sure clustering shared secrets are actually set. (Source: SecurityWeek)

item.title: Amazon decoys catch ARTEX-style agents hunting exposed LiteLLM, Dify, Langflow and RAGFlow installs for API keys
item.guid: 2026-11-20|https://thehackernews.com/2026/11/amazon-uncovers-ai-agent-campaign.html|Amazon decoys catch ARTEX-style agents hunting exposed LiteLLM, Dify, Langflow and RAGFlow installs for API keys
item.description: [CVE-2025-3248 · CVE-2026-28797] Amazon's MadPot honeypots, posing as LLM apps, logged autonomous attacker agents (moderate confidence ARTEX, operated by China-linked groups) that found exposed AI gateways and apps, pulled provider keys via default LiteLLM master keys, open management endpoints, SSRF and leaked env/source-map files, then validated and pooled the keys. Cloudflare separately saw ARTEX abuse a stolen CI/CD API token to fire hundreds of database dump requests and plant artex-* Workers. Treat AI gateways as production: require auth, change default master keys, patch Langflow to 1.3.0+ and RAGFlow to 0.25.0+, scope and expire API tokens, rotate exposed keys and watch AI provider spend. (Source: The Hacker News)

item.title: Nudge Security: business-platform AI agents mostly run on their creator's OAuth grants, so logs show the human
item.guid: 2026-11-20|https://www.helpnetsecurity.com/2026/11/19/ai-agents-employee-credentials-nudge-security-report/|Nudge Security: business-platform AI agents mostly run on their creator's OAuth grants, so logs show the human
item.description: Telemetry in Nudge Security's 2026 AI adoption report shows the median organization with agents runs seven of them across multiple platforms such as Rovo, Zapier, ChatGPT Agents and Cursor Automations, usually borrowing an employee's OAuth token or API key rather than having their own identity. That makes agent actions indistinguishable from the employee's in audit logs and widens the blast radius of a stolen token. Inventory agents and whose access they use, prune unused AI OAuth grants, rotate any secret pasted into a prompt, and move agent identities under your IdP where possible. (Source: Help Net Security)

item.title: Puppet report-processing deserialization bug (CVSS 9.4) is now in CISA KEV as attackers exploit it
item.guid: 2026-11-19|https://thehackernews.com/2026/11/hackers-exploiting-critical-puppet-rce.html|Puppet report-processing deserialization bug (CVSS 9.4) is now in CISA KEV as attackers exploit it
item.description: [Critical 9.4 · CVE-2026-115731 · CVE-2026-115732] CISA added CVE-2026-115731, an untrusted-deserialization flaw in Puppet's report handling that yields remote code execution, to KEV on November 17, with a December 1 federal deadline; no attack details have been shared. Exploitation needs a valid CA-signed agent certificate, so servers that auto-sign agent requests are most exposed, and a companion bug (CVE-2026-115732, CVSS 9.0) bypasses certificate-name authorization in Puppet and OpenVox. Upgrade to Puppet Enterprise 2026.0.1, 2025.12.1 or 2023.8.13 (Core 9.1.3 / 8.22.2) or the fixed OpenVox agent and server builds, tighten CA auto-signing, and check Puppet servers for compromise, since stolen CA keys would let an attacker impersonate managed hosts. (Source: The Hacker News)

item.title: Apache Roller XML-RPC deserialization RCE is under active attack, and the September fix missed versions 4.0.0-6.1.4
item.guid: 2026-11-19|https://thehackernews.com/2026/11/critical-apache-roller-rce-flaw-under.html|Apache Roller XML-RPC deserialization RCE is under active attack, and the September fix missed versions 4.0.0-6.1.4
item.description: [Critical 9.8 · CVE-2026-129448 · CVE-2026-82384] The Apache Software Foundation says CVE-2026-129448, an unauthenticated deserialization bug in Roller's XML-RPC endpoint, is being actively exploited; the endpoint unpacks vendor extension types before checking who is calling. It is the same flaw as September's CVE-2026-82384, which was scoped only to 6.1.5, and covers Roller 4.0.0 through 6.1.4. Upgrade to 6.1.6 or later; if you cannot, set enabledForExtensions to false in WEB-INF/web.xml or remove the /roller-services/xmlrpc servlet mapping and restart, because switching XML-RPC off in the admin UI does not stop older builds from deserializing the request. (Source: The Hacker News)

item.title: CISA KEV adds Synology DSM, LiteLLM guardrail sandbox escape, end-of-life Apache Axis 1.x and REDCap bugs
item.guid: 2026-11-19|https://securityonline.info/cisa-adds-4-exploited-flaws-kev-synology-litellm/|CISA KEV adds Synology DSM, LiteLLM guardrail sandbox escape, end-of-life Apache Axis 1.x and REDCap bugs
item.description: [Critical 9.8 · CVE-2024-10441 · CVE-2026-40217 · CVE-2026-90436 · CVE-2026-90817] CISA's November 18 KEV update covers an unauthenticated RCE in Synology DSM and BeeStation OS, a LiteLLM proxy bug where an authenticated user can escape the AST sandbox on the /guardrails/test_custom_code route, an unsafe-reflection RCE in Apache Axis 1.x triggered by a crafted SOAP Fault, and a REDCap code-injection flaw reachable with a public survey hash. Federal deadlines are November 21 for three of them and December 2 for LiteLLM. Patch DSM and REDCap to the fixed builds, run a LiteLLM build newer than April 8, 2026 and keep its admin routes off the internet, and plan to migrate off Axis 1.x, which is end-of-life and fixed only by an upstream commit. (Source: SecurityOnline)

item.title: 'nginx2root': public PoCs for a 10-year-old NGINX HTTP/2 bug show worker RCE, chained to host root via a kernel flaw
item.guid: 2026-11-19|https://thehackernews.com/2026/11/10-year-old-nginx-http2-flaw-lets.html|'nginx2root': public PoCs for a 10-year-old NGINX HTTP/2 bug show worker RCE, chained to host root via a kernel flaw
item.description: [Critical 9.2 · CVE-2026-123007 · CVE-2026-123633 · CVE-2026-123634 · CVE-2026-121810 · CVE-2026-113425] F5 fixed five NGINX flaws rated CVSS 4.0 9.2, led by CVE-2026-123007, an HTTP/2 flow-control error present since 1.9.5 in 2015; Rapid7, Wiz and Xint have published proof-of-concept code, and Xint chained it with a Linux SCTP kernel bug to reach root on cloud hosts. No in-the-wild exploitation is reported yet, and the attacks need ASLR bypassed, AVX-512 CPUs and sustained heavy HTTP/2 traffic. Upgrade to NGINX 1.31.9 or 1.30.7 (Plus 37.3.0.1 or 37.0.8.1) with a full restart rather than a reload, check distro packages separately, disable HTTP/2 and HTTP/3 if patching must wait, and block the sctp module where it is not needed. (Source: The Hacker News)

item.title: F5 ships hotfix-only patches for six critical BIG-IP data-plane overflows tied to specific iRule and APM setups
item.guid: 2026-11-19|https://thehackernews.com/2026/11/f5-warns-6-critical-big-ip-flaws-can.html|F5 ships hotfix-only patches for six critical BIG-IP data-plane overflows tied to specific iRule and APM setups
item.description: [Critical 9.8 · CVE-2026-123637 · CVE-2026-121805 · CVE-2026-120292 · CVE-2026-120285 · CVE-2026-116953 · CVE-2026-120722] Six unauthenticated stack overflows in BIG-IP's traffic microkernel can crash TMM and may allow code execution when a virtual server uses certain features, such as iRules calling PEM::subscriber, MR::message route, PSC::ip_address, GENERICMESSAGE::route or DNS::scrape, or an APM per-request policy with the Client Information and Endpoint Security agents. None is reported exploited, but fixes exist only as engineering hotfixes and there is no workaround. Audit virtual servers for those configurations, request and install the matching EHF for BIG-IP, BIG-IP Next for Kubernetes or CNF, and apply the regular releases that fix the lower-rated iControl and SAML bugs in the same batch. (Source: The Hacker News)

item.title: PHP Foundation pre-announces a critical security release for November 19, 14:00-14:30 UTC
item.guid: 2026-11-19|https://www.theregister.com/patches/2026/11/18/get-ready-for-another-critical-php-security-release-to-drop/5310911|PHP Foundation pre-announces a critical security release for November 19, 14:00-14:30 UTC
item.description: [Critical · CVE-2026-115560] The PHP Foundation says releases due Thursday fix bugs rated critical, though they need non-default configurations or uncommon setups. One is CVE-2026-115560, a session RCE that requires the serialize handler to be switched to 'php' at runtime with ini_set() before session_start() while session upload progress is enabled. Schedule the upgrade for as soon as the builds land, and until then set session.upload_progress.enabled=0 and check whether any app changes session.serialize_handler at runtime. (Source: The Register)

item.title: 'Trigram' fakes about 50 AI and crypto brands to get developers to run infostealers, using a forged commit and an IDE extension
item.guid: 2026-11-19|https://thehackernews.com/2026/11/trigram-campaign-impersonates-about-50.html|'Trigram' fakes about 50 AI and crypto brands to get developers to run infostealers, using a forged commit and an IDE extension
item.description: Stormshield tracks Trigram, which it links with high confidence to the UNK_DeadDrop cluster, as luring developers with fake job, conference and parcel sites that ask them to paste a 'technical check' command; the loader installs Node.js and runs an encrypted stealer in memory that takes browser data, wallets, SSH keys and .env files, then adds the Overlord RAT. Other routes include a forged October 31 commit to the antd-img-crop GitHub repo that adds a prebuild.js hook (the npm package was not touched) and a sideloaded VS Code/Cursor extension named google-dev-tools.google-update-support. Treat 'run this command' steps in hiring or event flows as hostile, review build hooks in cloned repos, and allow-list IDE extensions. (Source: The Hacker News)

item.title: Canonical opens an opt-in 'Edge' archive of AI-agent-written Ubuntu security backports, released before human review
item.guid: 2026-11-19|https://www.helpnetsecurity.com/2026/11/18/ubuntu-ai-security-patches-edge-archive/|Canonical opens an opt-in 'Edge' archive of AI-agent-written Ubuntu security backports, released before human review
item.description: Ubuntu Pro customers can now opt in to patches from Surge, a chain of agents that matches vulnerability reports to Ubuntu packages, pulls the upstream fix, has several models write competing backports and lets a panel of judge models pick one, escalating to a human only on deadlock or low confidence. Patches still go through Ubuntu's deterministic build tests, cover known userspace flaws only, and leave out the kernel, which moves to a two-week SRU cycle. Leave Edge off for production unless you can test the patches yourself, since enabling it moves the job of judging patch safety from Canonical to you. (Source: Help Net Security)

item.title: Arize Phoenix CVSS 10 flaw lets an unauthenticated GraphQL call leak env vars and PHOENIX_SECRET via chat templates
item.guid: 2026-11-19|https://www.rapid7.com/db/vulnerabilities/cve-2026-53998/|Arize Phoenix CVSS 10 flaw lets an unauthenticated GraphQL call leak env vars and PHOENIX_SECRET via chat templates
item.description: [Critical 10.0 · CVE-2026-53998] In the Arize Phoenix LLM observability platform, the applyChatTemplate GraphQL query passes attacker-supplied f-string templates to a formatter that does not block private attributes, so a crafted field can walk Python internals and read environment variables and module state. Leaking PHOENIX_SECRET would let an attacker forge admin sessions and decrypt stored credentials, and the endpoint needs no login on default installs. Rapid7 lists versions from 13.0.0 as affected and 15.7.0 as the fix; upgrade to the current release, keep Phoenix off the public internet, and rotate PHOENIX_SECRET and stored provider keys if it was exposed. (Source: Rapid7)

item.title: macOS 27.3 beta splits broad Mac permissions into narrower grants as Apple reacts to AI agents taking control of desktops
item.guid: 2026-11-19|https://thehackernews.com/2026/11/apple-tightens-macos-app-permissions-to.html|macOS 27.3 beta splits broad Mac permissions into narrower grants as Apple reacts to AI agents taking control of desktops
item.description: Apple is splitting the old Device Control and Data Access permission into System & App Protection Override and Accessibility, scoping Full Disk Access to chosen folders, offering an ask-every-time option, and showing an indicator when one app drives another. Apple ties the change to the risk of handing agent apps whole-Mac access; existing grants stay in place for now. Developers of agent and automation tools should handle folder-limited access in onboarding and apply for entitlements where needed, and Mac admins should review which apps hold broad grants. (Source: The Hacker News)

item.title: 'Java4Shell': AVX-512 Base64 decoder overflow in OpenJDK gives pre-auth RCE in Jenkins, Confluence, Keycloak and more
item.guid: 2026-11-18|https://www.sentinelone.com/blog/java4shell-vulnerability-in-openjdk-enables-rce-on-avx-512-cpus/|'Java4Shell': AVX-512 Base64 decoder overflow in OpenJDK gives pre-auth RCE in Jenkins, Confluence, Keycloak and more
item.description: [Critical 9.2 (CVSS 4.0) · CVE-2026-114938] Calif disclosed a memory-corruption bug in OpenJDK's optimised java.util.Base64 decoder that only runs on x86-64 CPUs with AVX-512 VBMI (recent Xeon and Zen 4+ EPYC/Ryzen; ARM64 is not affected): a crafted padded Base64 string overwrites adjacent heap memory, and Calif showed unauthenticated code execution in default setups of Jenkins, Jira, Confluence, Keycloak, Kafka, PingFederate, Artifactory and Spring Boot apps. It affects OpenJDK 17.0.6 and later plus the current Oracle 8/17/21/25/27 builds, and Oracle and OpenJDK shipped fixes in the November 17 Java update; no in-the-wild exploitation was reported at disclosure, but Wiz says it rebuilt a working exploit within two hours. Inventory every JVM including bundled and container runtimes, patch internet-facing and identity systems first, and where you cannot patch yet start x86-64 JVMs with -XX:UseAVX=2 to disable the vulnerable code path. (Source: SentinelOne)

item.title: Optimizely flaw let attackers plant skimmers, wallet swappers and iOS exploit kits in tags used by 178 big brands
item.guid: 2026-11-18|https://thehackernews.com/2026/11/hijacked-optimizely-scripts-served-card.html|Optimizely flaw let attackers plant skimmers, wallet swappers and iOS exploit kits in tags used by 178 big brands
item.description: On November 16 an attacker abused an undisclosed Optimizely Web Experimentation vulnerability to insert JavaScript into customers' Project JavaScript, so sites including BBC, CNN, Zoom, GitLab, HSBC and Salesforce served code that swapped crypto addresses, skimmed card data typed into first-party forms, and pushed Coruna/DarkSword exploit kits to older iPhones; Report URI found the payload in 188 of 1,611 snippets checked. Optimizely says the hole is fixed and injected code removed, and most snippets were clean by that evening. Teams using Optimizely should review project and experiment code for 1688360[.]cc, .icu hosts and atob( loaders, rotate tokens with write access, hunt logs from November 16 for 1688360[.]cc / 136.113.106[.]136, and keep third-party tags off checkout pages behind a strict CSP (allow-listing cdn.optimizely.com alone did not help). (Source: The Hacker News)

item.title: Microsoft's agent-framework on PyPI briefly shipped a .pth credential stealer hunting Azure, CI and GitHub OIDC tokens
item.guid: 2026-11-18|https://www.wiz.io/blog/malicious-version-of-microsofts-agent-framework-published-to-pypi|Microsoft's agent-framework on PyPI briefly shipped a .pth credential stealer hunting Azure, CI and GitHub OIDC tokens
item.description: Versions 1.26.1 and 1.26.2 of Microsoft's agent-framework Python package were uploaded straight to PyPI on November 17 (about 55 minutes live) without matching GitHub tags, and each dropped a .pth file that runs a stealer on every Python start, even if the package is never imported. It sweeps environment variables, /proc environ files, Azure CLI, Docker, npm, pip, git and Hugging Face credentials, managed-identity and Azure DevOps OIDC tokens, and in 1.26.2 GitHub Actions OIDC tokens, posting them to a webhook[.]site endpoint. Pin to 1.26.0, search lockfiles, images and runner logs for the bad versions and for agent_framework_meta.pth or af_runtime_diag.pth, and rotate every secret and federated credential reachable from any environment that installed them. (Source: Wiz)

item.title: Month-long spray of guest 'run file' requests abuses ScreenConnect CVE-2026-84869 against MSP servers
item.guid: 2026-11-18|https://www.securityweek.com/msp-screenconnect-servers-targeted-in-month-long-campaign/|Month-long spray of guest 'run file' requests abuses ScreenConnect CVE-2026-84869 against MSP servers
item.description: [Critical 9.9 · CVE-2026-84869] Huntress reports that since at least October 20 attackers have sent roughly 688,000 guest 'run file' requests for update*.bat files to 42 MSP ScreenConnect servers, exploiting a missing-authorization flaw that lets files run on a technician's machine during a session without any prompt; the batch file talks to a Telegram bot and installs a rogue ScreenConnect client.
